newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA PLANS TO CUT DEBTS OF STATE ENTERPRISES.
newsitem.headline: CHINA PLANS TO CUT DEBTS OF STATE ENTERPRISES.

text.p: China plans new measures to reduce the mounting liabilities of lumbering state enterprises and to ease the bad debts burdening state banks, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Monday.

The new measures would include allowing state banks to sell creditor rights over state firms to third parties as well as allowing more state firms to issue shares and use the proceeds to reduce debt with state banks, the newspaper said.
Under the measures, state banks could sell their creditor rights at a discount while the buyers would exchange the rights with state firms for shares, it said.
State banks losses resulting from the transfer of creditor rights would be covered by funds from their bad debt reserves, the newspaper said.

China also planned to establish investment funds to pool more money from domestic and foreign sources for its state sector, it said, adding that more state enterprises could trim debt by repaying banks with cash raised through stock issues.
Beijing has vowed to revive its state sector, whose economic clout has been rapidly eroded since late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping launched market-oriented economic reform in the late 1970s.

State banks are burdened with huge problem loans that have little chance of being recalled due to Beijing's previous policy of ordering banks to make loans to state firms based on policy needs and with little regard to creditworthiness of borrowers.
Standard & Poor's rating agency said on Monday that flawed or "impaired" loans in China's banking sector could total US$200 billion.
Chinese central bank officials declined to comment, but commercial bank officials said the figure was not so large.
"This figure sounds too big," an official of the Bank of China said.

"The burden on China's four big state banks is very heavy, but this is a historical problem," he said. "The bad debt problem is the legacy of China's long centrally planned economy that cannot be resolved just in a short time."
China's four state-owned commercial banks are the Bank of China, the China Construction Bank, the Agricultural Bank of china and the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China.
Officials have refused to reveal the amount of bad debt, saying this is a state secret.
